description: @wakeshift/sdk: define the events an MCP server offers, serve them as MCP Events, and emit them; Wakeshift wakes every subscribed agent conversation (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT and others). For @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.x and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.x, with Mastra and xmcp adapters.
rules: Read the app key from the WAKESHIFT_KEY environment variable (wst_ followed by 50 characters). Never hard-code it or commit it.
Install @wakeshift/sdk from npm, not as a file: dependency on a checkout, which can load a second copy of zod.
Import z from "zod", not "zod/v4": the MCP SDK refuses a schema that mixes the two.
Define every event with wake.defineEvent before calling wake.attach, which throws when no event is defined.

In your own tools, declare the events each one subscribes to: attached.events(name, { subscribes: [event] }, handler). call.subscribe takes only the listed events; a tool that subscribes to none passes subscribes: [].
With createMcpHandler, call wake.attach inside the function that makes each server.
wakeshift_wait is off by default. Turn it on with wake.attach(server, { tools: { wait: { enabled: true } } }) only on a stateless server whose requests may stay open 30 seconds or more.
Write event descriptions as plain statements of what happened, not instructions to the agent.
Pass an id to event.emit when the source may retry (a webhook delivery ID), so a retried emit is delivered once.
